text: Hello and welcome to live coverage of the Premier League clash between Newcastle United and Luton Town at St.
James' Park.
Newcastle ended a four-match losing run in the Premier League with a 3-1 win over Aston Villa in their last outing.

The Villans had won 16 of their previous 17 games at home in the top flight, but a brace from Fabian Schar and an own goal from Alex Moreno helped the Magpies to a comfortable three-goal lead before Ollie Watkins netted a consolation.
A third straight-away victory in all competitions lifted Eddie Howe's men into eighth position.
Newcastle are 14 points behind fourth-placed Tottenham, meaning their chances of qualifying for the Champions League for the second successive season is very unlikely.
However, they will still be hoping that a place in the Europa League or Europa Conference League is in their grasp.
Despite this, the Magpies must improve their form at St.
James' Park, with the hosts losing back-to-back fixtures against Nottingham Forest and Manchester City.
Luton are in good form in the Premier League and have won three of their last five matches to take themselves out of the relegation zone and into 17th position.
Securing two consecutive triumphs over Newcastle and Sheffield United at the start of the run, the Hatters lost 3-2 to Chelsea before collecting a point against Burnley.

However, Rob Edwards' men returned to winning ways with their most emphatic win of the season in their previous match, with a hat-trick from Elijah Adebayo and a goal from Chiedozie Ogbene helping them secure a 4-0 win over European hopefuls Brighton.
It was a special victory for Luton, with captain Tom Lockyer making his first appearance at Kenilworth Road since suffering a cardiac arrest in December's game at Bournemouth.
The visitors will now be looking to complete a famous double over Newcastle for the first time since the 1937-38 campaign.
Newcastle make one enforced change to the side that beat Villa 3-1 in their last Premier League outing.
Alexander Isak went off with a groin injury and is replaced in the attack by Almiron.
However, there is a double boost for the injury-hit Magpies, with Barnes and Wilson back on the bench after a spell on the sidelines.
Luton make one alteration to the team that thumped Brighton 4-0 in midweek.
Mengi comes into the defence and starts ahead of Burke.
Former Newcastle winger Townsend, who scored the only goal in the reverse fixture, is on the bench.
This is the first time Newcastle are hosting Luton in a league match since September 1992, beating them 2-0 in the second tier under Kevin Keegan.
Both teams are on the pitch and are ready to get started.
Luton get this Premier League clash under way.
The Hatters will be hoping for another fast start, with Rob Edwards' men scoring twice in the first 137 seconds against Brighton in their last outing.
Luton start with an aggressive press and are looking to win possession in Newcastle's half.
However, it opens the Hatters up for a counter, with Gordon racing down the right, cutting inside before having a pass across the box intercepted by Lokonga.
CHANCE! Luton are causing some early danger.
Ogbene uses his speed to get on the end of a direct pass down the right.
He gets beyond Burn and attempts to roll a pass across the box, but Schar slides across to make the interception.
Newcastle are passing the ball around their defensive third and are allowing Luton to come onto them.
Schar takes too long in possession and Clark tackles him, but it rolls harmlessly back to Dubravka.
GOALLLL! LONGSTAFF SCORES! 1-0 NEWCASTLE! The hosts take an early lead.
Miley collects possession just inside Luton's half and chips a superb pass down the right to Trippier.
The right-back gets to the byline and cuts it back to Longstaff, who arrives in the box and drives his low effort into the bottom-left corner.
Miley's lofted pass down the right is excellent and it is matched by the pace of Trippier, who surges into the open space.
The full-back then delivers an excellent cross into a dangerous area, with Longstaff burying his first-time strike.
Newcastle have lost just one of their last 17 Premier League games against promoted sides (winning nine and drawing seven), though it was their most recent match in the reverse fixture against Luton.
Indeed, Luton could be just the second promoted side to do the double over the Magpies in the last seven seasons, after Leeds in 2020-21.
Ogbene is showing some real intent down the right.
He bursts into the box and gets beyond Burn before cutting the ball back into the middle, but Schar clears it away for a throw-in.
Guimaraes is down just inside Luton's half and needs a few moments before returning to his feet.
He looks to be struggling slightly.
Howe will be hoping that it is nothing serious.
The battle between Ogbene and Burn on the right will be one to keep an eye on.
The Luton winger is much quicker than the Magpies defender and is looking to go past him at every opportunity.
Adebayo runs down the left and wins Luton's first corner.
Newcastle bring everyone back and load the box.
Doughty finds Morris with an outswinging cross, but his tame header is caught with ease by Dubravka.
Burn makes a mess of a heavy touch on the right and is put under pressure by Ogbene, who wins possession well in an advanced position.
However, he cannot get away from Burn, with the defender quickly winning it back.
Luton are sloppy in possession in their own half, with Newcastle winning it back on the left.
Almiron collects it and attempts to curl an inviting cross into the box, but Kaminski rushes off his line to claim it.
GOALLL! LUTON ARE LEVEL! 1-1! Barkley is over a deep free-kick inside Newcastle's half on the right and he whips a cross onto the head of Morris.
The striker knocks it across the box to Osho, who gets away from his maker and powers his header into the net.

events.action: powers his header into the net

text: Luton are always threatening from set-pieces and show their qualities again.
Morris gets above his maker and finds Osho, who makes no mistake with an emphatic header from close range.
GOALLLL! LONGSTAFF SCORES AGAIN! 2-1 NEWCASTLE! The Magpies are ahead again.
Gordon races away on the counter down the left and uses his pace to get beyond Osho.
The winger then drives into the box and cuts onto his right foot before having a shot saved by Kaminski.
However, Longstaff is quickest to the rebound to score.
Luton are winless in their last 21 league visits to the Magpies (drawing five and losing 16).
Trippier has a corner on the right and he curls an inswinging cross into the box.
However, it goes over the head of everyone and out for a goal-kick.
Osho was grabbing Botman and was fortunate not to be punished.
Kaminski is looking unconvincing in possession, with the Luton goalkeeper passing the ball straight out for a corner under pressure.
Trippier tries a clever pass towards the outside of the box, but Clark reads it and makes the interception.
Doughty loses possession in Luton's half to Murphy, who attempts to whip a right-footed cross into the box from the right.
However, Kaminski is quick off his line to catch it.
The Hatters will be punished if they continue to lose the ball in their defensive third.
Adebayo looks to dribble past Botman to get into the box on the right but is stopped by the centre-back.
He thinks he should have a free-kick, but the referee ignores his claims.
The striker then shows his frustrations and fouls Schar.
Gordon arrives on the edge of the box on the right and offloads a pass to Murphy.
He sets it across to Guimaraes, who makes a deep run from midfield to create an option, but he takes a heavy touch and the chance is gone.
Newcastle are having all the chances at the moment.
Trippier strolls down the right and looks for options, finding Murphy on the overlap.
He then cuts a pass across to Gordon, who makes a mess of the shot, sending his effort wide.
Ogbene trips an onrushing Miley next to the touchline on the left and gifts Newcastle a free-kick in a crossing position.
Trippier switches sides to take it, but his ball into the box is cleared away with ease.
Luton's second corner is taken on the right by Doughty.
However, his outswinging cross is headed away.
The Hatters retain possession but are forced back to the halfway line by Newcastle's press.
GOALLL! BARKLEY SCORES! 2-2! Luton equalises for the second time.
Barkley wins possession off Longstaff and drives towards the edge of the box before sliding a pass down the left to Doughty.
His low strike is saved by Dubravka, but Barkley is there to thump in the rebound.
Barkley has now scored six goals in 16 appearances in the Premier League against Newcastle.
He loves scoring against the Magpies and comes up with a valuable equaliser.
Adebayo has the ball on the right and directs a low cross towards Morris.
However, the striker is put under pressure by Botman and cannot get it under control.
Dubravka then claims it with ease.
There will be four minutes of additional time.
Morris gives away a needless foul just inside Newcastle's half with a push, giving the Magpies a chance to throw men forward towards the end of the first half.
However, Mengi heads it clear just inside Luton's box.
Newcastle pass their way out of pressure and build an attack down the right after a clever pass from Gordon.
Trippier and Murphy combine, with the latter sending a searching cross into the box that is put behind by Mengi.
HALF-TIME: NEWCASTLE UNITED 2-2 LUTON TOWN
Luton twice came from behind against Newcastle to send the teams into the break level at St.
James' Park with the score 2-2.
Longstaff netted the opener for the hosts inside seven minutes, getting onto the end of Trippier's low cross to power his low, first-time strike into the bottom-left corner.
Osho then replied with a header from close range before the Magpies regained the lead moments later.
Gordon made a surging run down the left before cutting into the box and unleashing a curling effort.
Kaminski pushed it away, but Longstaff was there to score the rebound for his second goal of the contest.
However, Barkley ensured that an entertaining first 45 minutes ended level.
He dispossessed Longstaff and rolled a pass down the left side of the box to Doughty, who had his low strike saved.
The ball dropped straight to the feet of Barkley, with the midfielder taking a touch to compose himself before thumping in the equaliser.
Luton created better opportunities before the break and created an xG (expected goals) of 1.27 compared to Newcastle's 0.99.
Barkley had their most touches (47) and completed 88.2 per cent of his passes in an impressive midfield display.
However, the Hatters must be more careful in the defensive third, as they have often gifted the ball to the Magpies, who haven't been able to capitalise.
As for the hosts, they will be disappointed with their lack of control at home.
Howe's men have had just 48.7 per cent of the possession, with most of their best opportunities coming from counters.
Howe makes a change before the restart to try and make Newcastle's attack more threatening.
He brings on Wilson to add a recognised striker, with the England international making his first appearance since December 26.
Gordon is off.
Newcastle get the ball rolling again.
Almiron twists in possession on the right and slides a fantastic throughball to Trippier, who races forward before going down under pressure from Doughty.
He wants a free-kick on the edge of the box, but nothing is given.
SAVE! Huge opportunity for Newcastle.
Wilson does brilliantly to collect the ball with his back to goal before flicking it around to Miley.
He then finds Murphy, who gets into the box and dribbles past a defender before having a low drive saved by the foot of Kaminski.
Ogbene brings the ball forward down the right, waiting for support before sliding a pass down the wing to Clark.
He attempts to loft a cross into the middle towards Adebayo, but it goes over his head and away from danger.
Murphy has a shot blocked just inside the box, but Newcastle retain possession through Miley, who gives it back to him.
The winger then gets beyond a defender before lashing a shot wide of the near post on the left.
PENALTY SHOUT! Luton have a free-kick on the edge of the box, but the Hatters want a penalty.
Ogbene drives beyond Burn on the right and gets past him before getting dragged back right on the edge.
Burn is shown a yellow card for dragging back Ogbene on the edge of the box.
The VAR check is ongoing for a possible penalty.
PENALTY TO LUTON! The Hatters have the chance to get themselves ahead.
Burn was dragging back Ogbene on the edge of the box, but the foul continued inside and a penalty is given.
Morris has the ball in his hand.
WHAT! Morris strikes the penalty to the right of the goal and into the net, but the referee isn't ready and Morris is forced to take it again.
GOALLL! MORRIS SCORES! 3-2 LUTON! The Hatters are ahead for the first time.
Morris takes a slow run before slotting his effort down the right side of the goal.
Dubravka dives the other way.
Lokonga is shown a yellow card after dragging back Guimaraes around the halfway mark.
GOALLL! ADEBAYO SCORES! 4-2 LUTON! The Hatters score again! Trippier advances forward and leaves Doughty plenty of space to run into.
He slides a pass across to Barkley, who is on the edge of the box.
The midfielder then rolls a pass down the right to Adebayo, who drives his low strike across the goal and into the bottom-left corner.
Barkley has been excellent for Luton and adds an assist to his goal.
He could shoot on the edge of the box but waits for the run of Adebayo, who is completely free and finishes clinically.
Barnes makes his first appearance since September after a serious injury.
He is on for Almiron in the attack.
Burn has had a torrid time at left-back and gave away a penalty for Luton's third goal.
The electric Livramento replaces him in the defence to try and add some attacking qualities.

Adebayo has scored seven goals in his last eight Premier League appearances and netted the Hatters’ first top-flight hat-trick since September 1990 (Lars Elstrup vs Norwich) in their 4-0 win over Brighton.
GOALLLLL! TRIPPIER GETS ONE BACK FOR NEWCASTLE! The hosts needed that! Miley finds Guimaraes on the left, with the midfielder curling a cross with the outside of his boot towards Trippier.
The right-back gets ahead of his marker and sends a first-time effort into the bottom-left corner.
Luton lead 4-3.
A moment of brilliance from Guimaraes.
He is on the corner of the box on the left and finds Trippier with an inventive cross with the outside of his boot.
Trippier makes a bursting run and scores to get Newcastle's third goal.
Luton make a change immediately after Newcastle's goal.
Mpanzu is on to replace Clark in this frantic contest.
Newcastle have lost their last two Premier League home games, as many as in their previous 16 at St James’ Park (winning 13 and drawing one).
They last lost three in a row between January and February 2021 under Steve Bruce.
They have the momentum and the home fans on their side, but Luton are still ahead.
Trippier is over a free-kick on the right in a crossing position.
Wilson attacks it and Barkley heads it into the air.
Kaminski pushes it away but not convincingly, with Schar's effort deflecting wide.

GOALLL! BARNES SCORES! 4-4! Newcastle come from two goals behind to level the score! Barnes receives possession from Miley on the edge of the box and shifts the ball onto his left foot before curling a low effort into the bottom-left corner.
He went for accuracy rather than power to find the equaliser.
Miley is involved again, this time with a short pass on the edge of the box.
However, the goal is all about Barnes, who curls his strike from range into the bottom-left corner.
Murphy makes a late slide tackle on Ogbene and is shown a yellow card.
WIDE! Newcastle are pushing for their fifth goal.
Murphy gets down the right and flashes an inviting cross into the box.
It is headed away from Wilson by Osho but straight to Barnes.
He looks to score his second off the bench, with his right-footed effort defecting off of Mengi and behind.
Morris scored Luton's third and is now coming off.
He hands the captain's armband to Mpanzu before coming off for Brown.
Doughty is also on his way off after an energetic performance on the left.
He is replaced by Burke, who started the last match.
Brown gets straight into the action, getting down the left of the box and towards the byline.
However, his cutback goes straight into the gloves of Dubravka.
WIDE! Schar drives through the middle of the pitch before rolling a pass down the left to Barnes.
He curls a low shot across the goal, with the ball taking a slight deflection.
Kaminski reacts quickly and pushes it behind.
Wilson protects the ball well from Osho and loops a pass over the top of Luton's defence, but Kaminski runs off his line to catch it.
OVER! What an opportunity for Murphy.
Guimaraes speeds down the left and looks to get his second assist with the outside of his right foot.
The ball flashes across the face of the goal and towards Murphy, but he shoots over from a tight angle.
Adebayo went down a few moments ago but is now back on his feet to come off.
Woodrow is on for the final few minutes to try and make an impression.
What an opportunity for the striker to score the winner.
Schar takes a quick free-kick in Newcastle's half and drives a pass forward to Wilson.
He accidentally trips Osho and gives away a free-kick after a tangle of legs.
Osho goes into the book after dragging back Wilson.
There will be 10 minutes of additional time.
There should be no surprise after four goals and VAR drama!
Newcastle have all the momentum and are pushing for the winner.
They still have seven minutes to score their fifth goal but are looking to put crosses into the box at every opportunity.
Luton have a height advantage and have dealt with the pressure well.
Ogbene and Woodrow play a clever one-two on the right, giving the former of the pair space to run into.
He gets to the byline and cuts a pass back towards Mpanzu, but Livramento makes an important covering run to make the interception.
Brown is down and receiving treatment after a collision.
However, he will be able to continue.
This will only further extend the added time and the drama.
Trippier trips Mpanzu and wins a free-kick in a crossing position for Luton.
Barkley's cross drops in the middle of the box before getting hacked away by the Newcastle defence.
CHANCE! What an opportunity for Luton to score the winner.
Barkley makes the most of a loose pass from Schar.
He has possession on the left and curls a right-footed cross over to Ogbene on the right side of the box.
He attempts a first-time volley, but Dubravka makes a simple save under pressure.
The allocated additional time has now ended, but the match continues.
Newcastle surge forward on the counter.
However, Luton get men back before Trippier's cross from the right is blocked.
FULL-TIME: NEWCASTLE UNITED 4-4 LUTON TWON
Newcastle came from two goals down in the second half to draw 4-4 with Luton in a Premier League classic at St.
James' Park.
The Hatters twice came from behind before the break to level the score.
Longstaff netted a brace, getting onto the end of Trippier's cutback to break the deadlock before reacting the quickest to a rebounded strike from Gordon to add his second.
However, the Hatters were resilient.
Osho headed in their first, with Barkley crashing in his strike from close range after Doughty's shot was pushed into his path.
Luton then gained control after scoring twice to go 4-2 ahead.
The referee pointed to the spot after a VAR check, with Burn pulling back Ogbene just inside the box.
Morris rolled in the spot-kick to put the visitors ahead before Adebayo added their fourth with a low strike into the bottom-left corner.
However, they couldn't hold onto their lead.
Trippier started the comeback with a goal before Barnes netted their leveller with an accurate strike from the edge into the bottom-left corner.
Next up, Newcastle travel to Nottingham Forest in the Premier League, with Luton hosting Sheffield United.
That's all, goodbye.
